threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think waiting for a bus is an option; real locals are masters of the night bike ride or the Uber shuffle.
Caught a whiff of jerk chicken from a late-night stall on the 35 last week. Best part of the ride was watching folks fight the urge to get off for a bite.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Sitting at the café, I watched a toddler barter their toy for a piece of cake. That’s when it hit me - this place really runs on smiles and sweet deals.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin will you see a group of punks arguing with a group of hipsters over the best currywurst late at night, while a stray cat watches. It's oddly charming.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they calmly step over the Muni delays caused by a dog on the tracks like it’s just another Tuesday.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full suit pull out a ukulele and start playing while waiting for the Muni. Only in the Tenderloin, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think ‘Gràcia’ means just Gaudí. They miss the quiet corners where neighbors gather, like at Plaça de la Virreina, away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always spot a recent arrival by the way they still marvel at the tiny balconies, trying to fit an entire garden on them.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it Dalston Junction instead of just 'The Junction'. You’re also clutching your Oyster card like it’s made of gold.
Last weekend on the 333, a guy serenaded the whole bus with a karaoke version of 'Wonderwall'. Even the driver couldn't help but chuckle.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was really here when my neighbor's cat started showing up on my balcony every morning, demanding breakfast like it owned the place.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a currywurst after a late-night rave, then find a quiet café open till dawn for a post-party espresso.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they’ve got a favorite taco truck and can recite all the BART delays without checking their phone.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, a saxophonist set up right next to a Muni stop. The chaos of the bus delay melted away as he played Coltrane. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think it’s all about the Gaudí sights here, but the real pulse of Gràcia is in the tiny plaques commemorating local artists you stumble upon.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll see them struggling with paella portions, ordering just one instead of the usual 'per persona.' They carry a Tupperware for leftovers, bless them.
